items.stem: Which term is defined as "a muscle or gland that carries out a response"?
items.answer: Effector
items.markingKey: Effector: a muscle or gland that carries out a response.

items.stem: Explain why reflex actions are important for survival.
items.answer: They are automatic and very fast, so the body responds to danger (e.g. heat, bright light) before damage occurs, without conscious thought.
items.markingKey: fast / automatic [1]; prevents harm [1] [2]

items.stem: Describe the events at a synapse when an impulse arrives.
items.answer: The impulse causes vesicles to release neurotransmitter into the gap; it diffuses across and binds to receptor molecules on the next neurone, starting a new impulse.
items.markingKey: vesicles release neurotransmitter [1]; diffuses across gap [1]; binds receptors / new impulse [1] [3]

items.stem: Mei measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. Results table. Number of practice attempts: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Distance fallen / cm, trial 1: 18.4, 12.6, 10.2, 8.6, 8.4; trial 2: 16.9, 13.1, 10.3, 9.2, 8.2; trial 3: 17.8, 13.1, 10.6, 8.9, 7.9. State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis.
items.answer: A line graph: number of practice attempts on the x-axis and mean distance fallen on the y-axis.
items.markingKey: line graph (continuous independent variable) [1]; number of practice attempts on x-axis and distance fallen on y-axis [1] [2]

items.stem: Felix measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. Results table. Number of practice attempts: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Distance fallen / cm, trial 1: 22, 15.1, 12.5, 11, 6.3; trial 2: 23.1, 16.9, 12.3, 11.3, 10.5; trial 3: 21.8, 16.9, 12.8, 11.4, 9.7. (a) Describe the trend shown by the results. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: (a) As the number of practice attempts increases, the distance fallen decreases (reaction time gets shorter), levelling off. (b) Use a computer reaction timer for more precise times.
items.markingKey: (a) correct overall pattern [1]; data quoted with units / turning point given [1] [2] (b) Any one from: use a computer reaction timer for more precise times; test several people and calculate a mean; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the number of practice attempts (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: Yusuf measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. Results table. Number of practice attempts: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Distance fallen / cm, trial 1: 20.4, 14.3, 12, 9.6, 8.9; trial 2: 21.1, 15.1, 11.2, 10, 5.1; trial 3: 20.8, 14.5, 11.4, 10.1, 9.5. (a) State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis. (b) Explain why catching the ruler is not a reflex action.
items.answer: (a) A line graph: number of practice attempts on the x-axis and mean distance fallen on the y-axis. (b) It involves conscious thought / the brain making a decision, and it is learned rather than automatic.
items.markingKey: (a) line graph (continuous independent variable) [1]; number of practice attempts on x-axis and distance fallen on y-axis [1] [2] (b) [2]

items.stem: Mateo measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. Results table. Number of practice attempts: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Distance fallen / cm, trial 1: 18.2, 13.5, 10.4, 8.3, 4.5; trial 2: 17.5, 12.2, 10.3, 8.9, 7.7; trial 3: 18, 12.5, 9.6, 8.3, 7.9. (a) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation. (b) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation.
items.answer: (a) Independent: number of practice attempts; dependent: distance fallen. (b) Same hand used; same starting position of fingers.
items.markingKey: (a) independent variable = number of practice attempts [1]; dependent variable = distance fallen [1] [2] (b) Any two from: same hand used; same starting position of fingers; same person dropping the ruler; no warning before the drop; same ruler [2]

items.stem: Omar measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. Results table. Number of practice attempts: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Distance fallen / cm, trial 1: 32.4, 15.1, 12.6, 10.4, 10.1; trial 2: 20.3, 16.1, 12.5, 9.9, 9.2; trial 3: 21.6, 14.9, 11.6, 10.9, 9.8. (a) Explain the results. (b) Calculate the reaction time for the first set of results using t = √(2d ÷ 9.8), with d in metres.
items.answer: (a) With practice, the brain becomes more efficient at processing the visual stimulus and sending impulses along motor neurones to the hand muscles, so the response is faster; there is a minimum time for impulses to travel and cross synapses. (b) 0.207 s
items.markingKey: (a) faster processing / pathway [1]; impulses to muscles [1]; limit set by nerve / synapse transmission [1] [3] (b) d = 0.2095 m [1]; t = √(2 × 0.2095 ÷ 9.8) = 0.207 s [1] [2]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "motor neurone"?
options: A chemical released at a synapse that diffuses across the gap and binds to receptors on the next neurone.
A means of automatically and rapidly integrating and coordinating stimuli with the responses of effectors.
A neurone that carries impulses from the central nervous system to an effector.
A muscle or gland that carries out a response.
items.answer: A neurone that carries impulses from the central nervous system to an effector.
items.markingKey: Motor neurone: a neurone that carries impulses from the central nervous system to an effector.

items.stem: What is the correct order of structures in a reflex arc?
options: receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
receptor → relay neurone → sensory neurone → effector → motor neurone
receptor → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → effector
effector → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → receptor
items.answer: receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
items.markingKey: Stimulus detected by receptor; impulse passes through CNS via relay neurone; effector responds.

items.stem: In the reflex response to touching a hot pan, what is the effector?
items.answer: muscles in the arm (biceps)
items.markingKey: Stimulus touching a hot pan; receptor heat / temperature receptors in the skin; effector muscles in the arm (biceps); response: hand pulled away.

items.stem: In the reflex response to a tap below the knee, what is the effector?
items.answer: thigh muscle (quadriceps)
items.markingKey: Stimulus a tap below the knee; receptor stretch receptors in the thigh muscle; effector thigh muscle (quadriceps); response: lower leg kicks.

items.stem: For the reflex response to stepping on a sharp object, name (a) the stimulus, (b) the receptor, (c) the effector and (d) describe the pathway of the impulse from receptor to effector.
items.answer: (a) stepping on a sharp object (b) pain receptors in the foot (c) leg muscles (d) receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone (CNS) → motor neurone → effector
items.markingKey: (a) [1] (b) pain receptors in the foot [1] (c) leg muscles [1] (d) correct sequence of three neurone types [2] [5]

items.stem: Amara measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. items.answer: (a) 14.07 cm (b) Use a computer reaction timer for more precise times.

items.answer: (a) Same hand used; same starting position of fingers. (b) With practice, the brain becomes more efficient at processing the visual stimulus and sending impulses along motor neurones to the hand muscles, so the response is faster; there is a minimum time for impulses to travel and cross synapses. items.stem: What is the name for "carries impulses from the retina to the brain"?
items.answer: Optic nerve
items.markingKey: Optic nerve: carries impulses from the retina to the brain.

items.stem: Explain how the eye focuses on a distant object.
items.answer: Ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments are pulled tight, the lens is pulled thin, refracting light less so it focuses on the retina.
items.markingKey: ciliary relax [1]; ligaments tight [1]; lens thin [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why the pupil reflex is important.
items.answer: It protects the retina from damage by bright light and lets more light in when it is dim so we can still see.

items.stem: Which part of the eye part of the retina with many cones, giving detailed colour vision?
items.answer: fovea
items.markingKey: Fovea: part of the retina with many cones, giving detailed colour vision.

items.stem: Omar walks from a dark room into bright sunlight. Describe the changes that occur in the eye and explain why they are needed.
items.answer: Circular muscles of the iris contract, radial relax; pupil constricts; this adjusts the light entering / keeps the image focused on the retina.
items.markingKey: muscle changes [2]; structure change [1]; reason [1] [4]

items.stem: An optometrist in Hanoi tests a patient's vision. The patient reads a chart 6 m away and then a card held 25 cm from the eyes. (a) Explain why the optometrist dims the lights before examining the retina. (b) State where light should be focused for the sharpest colour image and why.
items.answer: (a) In dim light the pupil dilates (radial muscles contract), so more of the retina can be seen. (b) On the fovea, which has the most cones.

items.stem: In bright light, what happens to the muscles of the iris?
options: Circular muscles contract and radial muscles relax
Radial muscles contract and circular muscles relax
items.answer: Circular muscles contract and radial muscles relax
items.markingKey: Pupil constricts, reducing light entering.

items.stem: Explain why we cannot see colours well in dim light.
items.answer: Cones need bright light to work; in dim light only rods respond, and rods do not distinguish colour.

items.stem: Pupil diameter was measured at different light intensities: 10 lux: 5.5 mm, 100 lux: 4.5 mm, 500 lux: 3.6 mm, 1000 lux: 3.4 mm, 5000 lux: 2.7 mm. (a) Describe the trend. (b) Name the muscles that contract to make the pupil smaller. (c) Calculate the percentage decrease in diameter from 10 to 5000 lux.
items.answer: (a) As light intensity increases, pupil diameter decreases (from 5.5 to 2.7 mm). (b) circular muscles of the iris (c) 50.9%
items.markingKey: (a) trend with data [1] (b) circular muscles [1] (c) (5.5 − 2.7) ÷ 5.5 × 100 = 50.9% [2] [4]

items.stem: Tomás walks from bright sunlight into a dark cinema. Describe the changes that occur in the eye and explain why they are needed.
items.answer: Radial muscles contract, circular relax; pupil dilates; this adjusts the light entering / keeps the image focused on the retina.
items.markingKey: muscle changes [2]; structure change [1]; reason [1] [4]

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "a hormone from the adrenal glands that prepares the body for fight or flight"?
items.answer: Adrenaline
items.markingKey: Adrenaline: a hormone from the adrenal glands that prepares the body for fight or flight.

items.stem: Explain how the effects of adrenaline help a person escape danger.
items.answer: Higher heart and breathing rates deliver more oxygen and glucose to muscles; blood glucose rises (glycogen breakdown); more respiration and energy release for muscle contraction.
items.markingKey: more O₂ / glucose to muscles [1]; more respiration / energy [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the response to a hormone is slower than a nervous response.
items.answer: Hormones are carried in the blood, which takes time to reach target organs; nerve impulses travel rapidly along neurones.

items.stem: Which gland secretes oestrogen and progesterone?
items.answer: ovaries
items.markingKey: Ovaries → oestrogen and progesterone.

items.stem: Compare nervous and hormonal control under these headings: duration of effect, form of signal, speed.
items.answer: duration of effect: nervous short, hormonal longer-lasting; form of signal: nervous electrical impulses, hormonal chemicals (hormones); speed: nervous fast, hormonal slower
items.markingKey: duration of effect [1]; form of signal [1]; speed [1] [3]

items.stem: A student in Bangkok hears a loud bang behind her. She jumps immediately, and for several minutes afterwards her heart pounds and her hands shake. (a) Explain why the jump happens immediately but the pounding heart lasts for several minutes. (b) Describe two other effects of adrenaline on the body.
items.answer: (a) The jump is a nervous response (fast impulses); the pounding heart is due to adrenaline in the blood, which takes time to be broken down, so its effect lasts longer. (b) Increased breathing rate; dilated pupils; increased blood glucose.
items.markingKey: (a) nervous fast [1]; hormone in blood, lasts longer [1] [2] (b) [2]

items.stem: Explain why a hormone only affects its target organs although it travels throughout the body.
items.answer: Only target cells have receptors with a shape complementary to the hormone.

items.stem: Tariq writes in a revision note: "Hormones travel along nerves to their target organs." Identify the error and write a correct statement.
items.answer: Hormones are carried by the blood plasma.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Hormones are carried by the blood plasma. [2]

items.stem: Before a parachute jump, a student's heart rate rose from 71 to 124 beats/min and blood glucose rose from 4.6 to 6.9 mmol/dm³. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in heart rate. (b) Name the hormone responsible and the gland that secretes it. (c) Explain the advantage of the rise in blood glucose.
items.answer: (a) 75% (b) adrenaline; adrenal glands (c) more glucose for respiration in muscles, releasing more energy for fight or flight.
items.markingKey: (a) (124 − 71) ÷ 71 × 100 = 75% [2] (b) adrenaline [1]; adrenal glands [1] (c) glucose for respiration / energy for muscles [1] [5]

items.stem: A student in Cairo hears a loud bang behind her. She jumps immediately, and for several minutes afterwards her heart pounds and her hands shake. (a) Describe two other effects of adrenaline on the body. (b) Compare nervous and hormonal control, giving three differences.
items.answer: (a) Increased breathing rate; dilated pupils; increased blood glucose. (b) Nervous: electrical impulses, along neurones, fast, short-lived. Hormonal: chemicals, in blood, slower, longer-lasting.

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "clinostat"?
options: A plant hormone made in the shoot tip that diffuses through the plant and stimulates cell elongation.
A response in which parts of a plant grow towards or away from gravity.
A slowly rotating device used to remove the effect of a one-sided stimulus such as gravity on a plant.
A response in which parts of a plant grow towards or away from the direction from which light is coming.
items.answer: A slowly rotating device used to remove the effect of a one-sided stimulus such as gravity on a plant.
items.markingKey: Clinostat: a slowly rotating device used to remove the effect of a one-sided stimulus such as gravity on a plant.

items.stem: Explain how auxin causes a shoot to bend towards light.
items.answer: Auxin is made in the tip and moves to the shaded side; it stimulates cell elongation there, so the shaded side grows faster and the shoot bends towards the light.
items.markingKey: auxin to shaded side [1]; cell elongation [1]; unequal growth / bending [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain the advantage of positive phototropism to a seedling.
items.answer: Leaves receive more light for photosynthesis, so more glucose is made for growth.

items.stem: Noah grew cress seedlings in boxes with a hole on one side, and measured the angle of bending of the shoots towards the light after 3 days at different distances from a lamp. Results table. Distance of lamp / cm: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. Angle of bending / °, trial 1: 45, 33, 25, 19, 15; trial 2: 45, 34, 25, 20, 23; trial 3: 45, 33, 26, 19, 16. Describe a suitable control for this investigation and explain why it is needed.
items.answer: Seedlings grown in a box with light from all sides (or in darkness) — they grow straight, showing bending is caused by one-sided light.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: control described; 1 mark: shows that the change is caused by the independent variable [2]

items.stem: Yusuf grew cress seedlings in boxes with a hole on one side, and measured the angle of bending of the shoots towards the light after 3 days at different distances from a lamp. Results table. Distance of lamp / cm: 25, 50, 75, 100. Angle of bending / °, trial 1: 47, 35, 25, 18; trial 2: 50, 35, 25, 19; trial 3: 47, 20, 25, 18. (a) Calculate the mean angle of bending at 100 cm, ignoring any anomalous result. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: (a) 18.3 ° (b) Use a protractor on photographs to measure angles more accurately.
items.markingKey: (a) (18 + 19 + 18) ÷ 3 [1] = 18.3 ° [1] [2] (b) Any one from: use a protractor on photographs to measure angles more accurately; use more seedlings per box and calculate the mean; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the distance of lamp (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: Arjun grew cress seedlings in boxes with a hole on one side, and measured the angle of bending of the shoots towards the light after 3 days at different distances from a lamp. Results table. Distance of lamp / cm: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. Angle of bending / °, trial 1: 43, 33, 24, 19, 15; trial 2: 42, 47, 26, 19, 15; trial 3: 41, 33, 25, 19, 15. (a) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation. (b) Describe a suitable control for this investigation and explain why it is needed.
items.answer: (a) Type and age of seedlings; temperature. (b) Seedlings grown in a box with light from all sides (or in darkness) — they grow straight, showing bending is caused by one-sided light.
items.markingKey: (a) Any two from: type and age of seedlings; temperature; water given; time of exposure; size of the hole [2] (b) 1 mark: control described; 1 mark: shows that the change is caused by the independent variable [2]

items.stem: Explain why a seedling placed on its side on a clinostat grows straight.
items.answer: Rotation means gravity acts equally on all sides, so auxin is evenly distributed and growth is even.

items.stem: A shoot tip is covered with a foil cap and lit from one side. Explain why the shoot does not bend.
items.answer: The tip detects light; with the tip covered, auxin is not redistributed to one side, so growth is even.

items.stem: Predict and explain the growth of a shoot on a slowly rotating clinostat, lit from one side.
items.answer: Grows straight: all sides receive light equally.
items.markingKey: prediction [1]; explanation referring to auxin / tip [2] [3]

items.stem: Grace grew cress seedlings in boxes with a hole on one side, and measured the angle of bending of the shoots towards the light after 3 days at different distances from a lamp. Results table. Distance of lamp / cm: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. Angle of bending / °, trial 1: 51, 39, 29, 23, 17; trial 2: 75, 40, 30, 22, 18; trial 3: 49, 40, 30, 23, 17. (a) Explain the results. (b) State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis.
items.answer: (a) With brighter light (closer lamp) the difference in light between the two sides is greater; more auxin moves to the shaded side, causing more cell elongation there and greater bending. (b) A line graph: distance of lamp on the x-axis and mean angle of bending on the y-axis.
items.markingKey: (a) auxin on shaded side [1]; cell elongation [1]; greater one-sided light causes more bending [1] [3] (b) line graph (continuous independent variable) [1]; distance of lamp on x-axis and angle of bending on y-axis [1] [2]

items.stem: Why can impulses only travel in one direction across a synapse?
options: The second neurone has no membrane
The synapse is a solid connection
Neurotransmitter is released only from one side and receptors are only on the other
items.answer: Neurotransmitter is released only from one side and receptors are only on the other
items.markingKey: Vesicles are in the presynaptic neurone; receptor proteins are on the postsynaptic membrane.

items.stem: Explain why some drugs that block receptor proteins at synapses can cause paralysis.
items.answer: Neurotransmitter cannot bind, so impulses are not passed to motor neurones / muscles; muscles cannot contract.
items.markingKey: blocks binding [1]; no impulse to muscle [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the relay neurone is found in the spinal cord in a reflex arc.
items.answer: The impulse passes from sensory to motor neurone through the spinal cord without first going to the brain, which makes the response quicker.
items.markingKey: shortest pathway / via spinal cord [1]; faster response [1] [2]

items.stem: An impulse travels 0.8 m along a motor neurone from the spinal cord to a foot muscle in 20 milliseconds. Calculate the speed of the impulse in m/s.
items.answer: 40 m/s

items.stem: Amara measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. Results table. Number of practice attempts: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Distance fallen / cm, trial 1: 19.9, 14, 12, 10.5, 9.3; trial 2: 21.4, 14.6, 11.6, 9.6, 9.5; trial 3: 13.1, 15.6, 11.4, 10.2, 9.4. State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation.
items.answer: Same hand used; same starting position of fingers.
items.markingKey: Any two from: same hand used; same starting position of fingers; same person dropping the ruler; no warning before the drop; same ruler [2]

items.stem: Priya accidentally touches a cactus spine in a garden in Riyadh and pulls the hand away before feeling any pain. (a) Name the type of response and explain why it is useful. (b) Explain why the pain is felt after the hand has moved.
items.answer: (a) A reflex action: rapid and automatic, reducing damage. (b) The impulse also travels up the spinal cord to the brain, a longer pathway; conscious awareness takes longer than the reflex.

items.stem: To focus on a near object, the lens becomes
items.answer: more rounded (fatter)
items.markingKey: Ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken, lens rounds up and refracts more.

items.stem: Explain why an image falling on the blind spot is not seen.
items.answer: There are no rods or cones there, because the optic nerve leaves the eye at that point.

items.stem: Which part of the eye contract or relax to change the shape of the lens?
items.answer: ciliary muscles
items.markingKey: Ciliary muscles: contract or relax to change the shape of the lens.

items.stem: Pupil diameter was measured at different light intensities: 10 lux: 5.7 mm, 100 lux: 4.6 mm, 500 lux: 3.8 mm, 1000 lux: 3.5 mm, 5000 lux: 2.7 mm. (a) Describe the trend. (b) Name the muscles that contract to make the pupil smaller. (c) Calculate the percentage decrease in diameter from 10 to 5000 lux.
items.answer: (a) As light intensity increases, pupil diameter decreases (from 5.7 to 2.7 mm). (b) circular muscles of the iris (c) 52.6%
items.markingKey: (a) trend with data [1] (b) circular muscles [1] (c) (5.7 − 2.7) ÷ 5.7 × 100 = 52.6% [2] [4]

items.stem: An optometrist in Kathmandu tests a patient's vision. The patient reads a chart 6 m away and then a card held 25 cm from the eyes. (a) Describe the changes in the eye when the patient changes focus from the chart to the card. (b) State where light should be focused for the sharpest colour image and why.
items.answer: (a) Ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken, lens becomes more rounded, refracts light more. (b) On the fovea, which has the most cones.

items.stem: What is the name for "the response to danger or stress controlled by adrenaline"?
items.answer: Fight or flight
items.markingKey: Fight or flight: the response to danger or stress controlled by adrenaline.

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why the response to a hormone is slower than a nervous response. (b) Explain why a hormone only affects its target organs although it travels throughout the body.
items.answer: (a) Hormones are carried in the blood, which takes time to reach target organs; nerve impulses travel rapidly along neurones. (b) Only target cells have receptors with a shape complementary to the hormone.

items.stem: Which gland secretes oestrogen and progesterone?
items.answer: ovaries
items.markingKey: Ovaries → oestrogen and progesterone.

items.stem: Before a parachute jump, a student's heart rate rose from 75 to 132 beats/min and blood glucose rose from 4.9 to 7.6 mmol/dm³. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in heart rate. (b) Name the hormone responsible and the gland that secretes it. (c) Explain the advantage of the rise in blood glucose.
items.answer: (a) 76% (b) adrenaline; adrenal glands (c) more glucose for respiration in muscles, releasing more energy for fight or flight.
items.markingKey: (a) (132 − 75) ÷ 75 × 100 = 76% [2] (b) adrenaline [1]; adrenal glands [1] (c) glucose for respiration / energy for muscles [1] [5]

items.stem: A student in Madrid hears a loud bang behind her. She jumps immediately, and for several minutes afterwards her heart pounds and her hands shake. (a) Explain why the jump happens immediately but the pounding heart lasts for several minutes. (b) Name the gland that releases adrenaline and state how adrenaline reaches the heart. (c) Describe two other effects of adrenaline on the body.
items.answer: (a) The jump is a nervous response (fast impulses); the pounding heart is due to adrenaline in the blood, which takes time to be broken down, so its effect lasts longer. (b) Adrenal glands; carried in the blood plasma. (c) Increased breathing rate; dilated pupils; increased blood glucose.
items.markingKey: (a) nervous fast [1]; hormone in blood, lasts longer [1] [2] (b) [2] (c) [2]

items.stem: Arjun writes in a revision note: "Auxin makes cells divide faster on the lit side." Identify the error and write a correct statement.
items.answer: Auxin moves to the shaded side, where it stimulates cell elongation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Auxin moves to the shaded side, where it stimulates cell elongation. [2]

items.stem: Hana writes in a revision note: "Plants grow towards light because light pulls them." Identify the error and write a correct statement.
items.answer: Auxin redistribution causes the shaded side to grow faster, so the shoot bends towards the light.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Auxin redistribution causes the shaded side to grow faster, so the shoot bends towards the light. [2]

items.stem: Predict the growth of a shoot lit from the left with a mica sheet inserted vertically below the tip on the shaded side.
options: does not grow / grows very little
items.answer: grows straight / little bending
items.markingKey: Grows straight / little bending: mica stops auxin moving down the shaded side.

items.stem: Bean seeds were germinated in damp cotton wool in a dark cupboard in Madrid. Some were placed horizontally; some were placed on a clinostat. (a) Explain why the seeds on the clinostat grow horizontally. (b) Explain the advantage of gravitropism to the root of a germinating seed.
items.answer: (a) Rotation means gravity acts on all sides equally, so there is no unequal auxin distribution. (b) Roots grow down into the soil to anchor the plant and reach water and mineral ions.

items.stem: What makes up the central nervous system?
items.answer: The brain and spinal cord
items.markingKey: The CNS is brain + spinal cord; nerves form the peripheral nervous system.

items.stem: A student in Accra states: "Impulses jump across synapses as electricity." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Neurotransmitter chemicals diffuse across the synaptic gap.

items.stem: An impulse travels 1.5 m along a motor neurone from the spinal cord to a foot muscle in 10 milliseconds. Calculate the speed of the impulse in m/s.

Mei measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. Results table. Number of practice attempts: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Distance fallen / cm, trial 1: 19.4, 13.3, 10.7, 9.5, 8.6; trial 2: 20.2, 14.5, 10.5, 9.3, 9; trial 3: 18.6, 14.4, 10.7, 9.3, 9. Describe the trend shown by the results.
items.answer: As the number of practice attempts increases, the distance fallen decreases (reaction time gets shorter), levelling off.
items.markingKey: correct overall pattern [1]; data quoted with units / turning point given [1] [2]

items.stem: Ravi measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. Results table. Number of practice attempts: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Distance fallen / cm, trial 1: 20.7, 13.9, 11.3, 9.3, 9; trial 2: 20.8, 13.8, 10.7, 10.3, 13.5; trial 3: 19, 13.7, 11, 9.8, 8.7. (a) Calculate the mean distance fallen after 20 practice attempts, ignoring any anomalous result. (b) Calculate the reaction time for the first set of results using t = √(2d ÷ 9.8), with d in metres.
Which cells in the retina allow colour vision?
items.answer: Cones
items.markingKey: Cones (three types) work in bright light; rods are sensitive in dim light.

items.stem: A student in Cape Town states: "The pupil gets smaller in dim light." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: The pupil dilates (gets larger) in dim light to let more light in.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: The pupil dilates (gets larger) in dim light to let more light in. [2]

items.stem: Which part of the eye carries impulses from the retina to the brain?
items.answer: optic nerve
items.markingKey: Optic nerve: carries impulses from the retina to the brain.

items.stem: Pupil diameter was measured at different light intensities: 10 lux: 6.0 mm, 100 lux: 4.9 mm, 500 lux: 4.4 mm, 1000 lux: 4.0 mm, 5000 lux: 3.3 mm. (a) Describe the trend. (b) Name the muscles that contract to make the pupil smaller. (c) Calculate the percentage decrease in diameter from 10 to 5000 lux.
items.answer: (a) As light intensity increases, pupil diameter decreases (from 6.0 to 3.3 mm). (b) circular muscles of the iris (c) 45%
items.markingKey: (a) trend with data [1] (b) circular muscles [1] (c) (6.0 − 3.3) ÷ 6.0 × 100 = 45% [2] [4]

items.stem: An optometrist in Nairobi tests a patient's vision. The patient reads a chart 6 m away and then a card held 25 cm from the eyes. (a) Describe the changes in the eye when the patient changes focus from the chart to the card. (b) Explain how information from the retina reaches the brain.
items.answer: (a) Ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken, lens becomes more rounded, refracts light more. (b) Rods and cones generate impulses carried along sensory neurones in the optic nerve to the brain.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "a ductless gland that secretes hormones directly into the blood"?
items.answer: Endocrine gland
items.markingKey: Endocrine gland: a ductless gland that secretes hormones directly into the blood.

items.stem: Ines says: "Hormones travel along nerves to their target organs." Explain whether Ines is correct.
items.answer: Hormones are carried by the blood plasma.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Hormones are carried by the blood plasma. [2]

items.stem: Which gland secretes FSH, LH and ADH?
items.answer: pituitary gland
items.markingKey: Pituitary gland → FSH, LH and ADH.

items.stem: Before a parachute jump, a student's heart rate rose from 68 to 97 beats/min and blood glucose rose from 4.6 to 6.6 mmol/dm³. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in heart rate. (b) Name the hormone responsible and the gland that secretes it. (c) Explain the advantage of the rise in blood glucose.
items.answer: (a) 43% (b) adrenaline; adrenal glands (c) more glucose for respiration in muscles, releasing more energy for fight or flight.
items.markingKey: (a) (97 − 68) ÷ 68 × 100 = 43% [2] (b) adrenaline [1]; adrenal glands [1] (c) glucose for respiration / energy for muscles [1] [5]

items.stem: Grace measured reaction time by catching a falling ruler. The distance the ruler fell before being caught was recorded for five attempts each after different numbers of practice attempts. Results table. Number of practice attempts: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Distance fallen / cm, trial 1: 22.3, 16, 12.6, 11.5, 9.7; trial 2: 12.9, 16.8, 12.1, 10.3, 9.7; trial 3: 23.5, 15.3, 12.7, 11.2, 9.5. (a) Identify the anomalous result in the table and state what should be done with it. (b) Calculate the mean distance fallen after 0 practice attempts, ignoring any anomalous result. (c) Describe the trend shown by the results.
items.answer: (a) Trial 2 after 0 practice attempts (12.9 cm); it should be ignored when calculating the mean (or repeated). (b) 22.9 cm (c) As the number of practice attempts increases, the distance fallen decreases (reaction time gets shorter), levelling off.
items.markingKey: (a) trial 2 after 0 practice attempts identified [1]; ignore / repeat it [1] [2] (b) (22.3 + 23.5) ÷ 2 [1] = 22.9 cm [1] [2] (c) correct overall pattern [1]; data quoted with units / turning point given [1] [2]

items.stem: Samuel says: "Auxin makes cells divide faster on the lit side." Explain whether Samuel is correct.
items.answer: Auxin moves to the shaded side, where it stimulates cell elongation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Auxin moves to the shaded side, where it stimulates cell elongation. [2]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain the advantage of positive phototropism to a seedling. (b) Explain why a seedling placed on its side on a clinostat grows straight.
items.answer: (a) Leaves receive more light for photosynthesis, so more glucose is made for growth. (b) Rotation means gravity acts equally on all sides, so auxin is evenly distributed and growth is even.

items.stem: Kenji grew cress seedlings in boxes with a hole on one side, and measured the angle of bending of the shoots towards the light after 3 days at different distances from a lamp. Results table. Distance of lamp / cm: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. Angle of bending / °, trial 1: 48, 36, 29, 14, 17; trial 2: 50, 37, 29, 22, 17; trial 3: 50, 37, 29, 22, 18. Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: Use a protractor on photographs to measure angles more accurately.
items.markingKey: Any one from: use a protractor on photographs to measure angles more accurately; use more seedlings per box and calculate the mean; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the distance of lamp (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: Grace grew cress seedlings in boxes with a hole on one side, and measured the angle of bending of the shoots towards the light after 3 days at different distances from a lamp. Results table. Distance of lamp / cm: 25, 50, 75, 100. Angle of bending / °, trial 1: 44, 33, 23, 16; trial 2: 45, 33, 23, 17; trial 3: 44, 31, 23, 10. (a) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation. (b) Describe the trend shown by the results.
items.answer: (a) Type and age of seedlings; temperature. (b) As the distance of lamp increases, the angle of bending decreases (from 44.33 to 16.5).
